statement: Let M = 1000000007. Define S(arr) = sum over all pairs (l, r) with 0 <= l <= r < n of min{ arr[k] | l <= k <= r }; the inner minimum is over a nonempty contiguous segment. Whenever sum_subarray_mins arr returns a result r, r = S(arr) mod M, i.e. r is the unique integer with 0 <= r < M such that S(arr) - r is divisible by M.
preconditions: arr is a slice of 64-bit integers with length n, where 1 <= n <= 30000, and 1 <= arr[i] <= 30000 for every 0 <= i < n.

statement: For every arr satisfying the preconditions, sum_subarray_mins arr returns a result r; it does not fail (no arithmetic overflow, indexing error, or panic).
preconditions: arr is a slice of 64-bit integers with length n, where 1 <= n <= 30000, and 1 <= arr[i] <= 30000 for every 0 <= i < n.

statement: Whenever sum_subarray_mins arr returns r, 0 <= r < 1000000007.
preconditions: arr is a slice of 64-bit integers with length n, where 1 <= n <= 30000, and 1 <= arr[i] <= 30000 for every 0 <= i < n.

statement: Whenever sum_subarray_mins arr returns r, r = (c * n * (n + 1) / 2) mod 1000000007, where n(n+1)/2 is the exact number of nonempty contiguous subarrays.
preconditions: n = len(arr), 1 <= n <= 30000, and there is an integer c with 1 <= c <= 30000 such that arr[i] = c for every 0 <= i < n.

statement: Whenever sum_subarray_mins arr returns r, r = (sum_{i=0}^{n-1} arr[i] * (n - i)) mod 1000000007.
preconditions: n = len(arr), 1 <= n <= 30000, 1 <= arr[i] <= 30000 for every i, and arr[0] < arr[1] < ... < arr[n-1].

statement: Whenever sum_subarray_mins arr returns r, r = (sum_{i=0}^{n-1} arr[i] * (i + 1)) mod 1000000007.
preconditions: n = len(arr), 1 <= n <= 30000, 1 <= arr[i] <= 30000 for every i, and arr[0] > arr[1] > ... > arr[n-1].

statement: Whenever sum_subarray_mins arr returns r and sum_subarray_mins rev returns r_rev, r = r_rev.
preconditions: n = len(arr), 1 <= n <= 30000, 1 <= arr[i] <= 30000 for every i. Let rev be the slice of length n with rev[i] = arr[n - 1 - i] for every 0 <= i < n.

statement: Whenever sum_subarray_mins arr returns r and sum_subarray_mins arr2 returns r2, r2 is congruent to r + c * (n * (n + 1) / 2) modulo 1000000007.
preconditions: arr and arr2 are slices of the same length n, with 1 <= n <= 30000 and all their entries in [1, 30000]. There is an integer c such that arr2[i] = arr[i] + c for every 0 <= i < n.

statement: Whenever sum_subarray_mins arr returns r and sum_subarray_mins arr2 returns r2, r2 is congruent to c * r modulo 1000000007.
preconditions: arr and arr2 are slices of the same length n, with 1 <= n <= 30000 and all their entries in [1, 30000]. There is an integer c with c >= 1 such that arr2[i] = c * arr[i] for every 0 <= i < n.

statement: Whenever sum_subarray_mins arr returns r and sum_subarray_mins arr2 returns r2, r2 is congruent to r + c * (n + 1) modulo 1000000007.
preconditions: arr has length n with 1 <= n <= 29999 (so arr2 has length n+1 <= 30000), arr2 has length n+1, all entries of arr and arr2 are in [1, 30000], arr2[i] = arr[i] for 0 <= i < n, and arr2[n] = c where 1 <= c <= 30000 and c <= arr[i] for every 0 <= i < n.

statement: Whenever sum_subarray_mins arr returns r and sum_subarray_mins arr2 returns r2, r2 is congruent to r + c + sum_{l=0}^{n-1} sufmin(l) modulo 1000000007.
preconditions: arr has length n with 1 <= n <= 29999 (so arr2 has length n+1 <= 30000), arr2 has length n+1, all entries of arr and arr2 are in [1, 30000], arr2[i] = arr[i] for 0 <= i < n, and arr2[n] = c where 1 <= c <= 30000 and c >= arr[i] for every 0 <= i < n. For 0 <= l < n let sufmin(l) = min{ arr[k] | l <= k < n }.
